root.name: Ruy Lopez: Bulgarian Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a5

overview: Black plays 3...a5, preventing Bxc6 ideas and keeping the pin from being resolved on White's terms. White usually continues 4.Bxc6 dxc6 5.Nxe5 Qd4 or 4.c3 and the game goes on as a normal Ruy Lopez. The move is rare and I am not sure of the main continuation.

white_ideas.idea: Build the c3 and d4 centre with O-O and Re1
Exchange on c6 to damage Black's pawns

black_ideas.idea: Support b4 and the knight with ...Nf6 and ...Be7
Use ...a5 to hold the bishop from a4

typical_structures.structure: Open Game structure with the bishop on b5 held

character.notes: Normal Ruy Lopez development with no forced tactics early.

structure.notes: Centre tension on e4 and e5.

character.reason: A normal Ruy Lopez set-up without forcing play.

level.reason: Ruy Lopez ideas rather than memorisation.

plans.reason: White plays for a normal centre.
